To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Monte Carlo simulations can be performed with realistic input distributions and that this approach is useful to assess the impact of the detector design on image quality and to optimize the acquisition and processing protocols.
Monte Carlo simulations can be performed with high accuracy and that the input activity distribution can be derived from patient images.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new techniques for the simulation of emission tomography images.
the use of Monte Carlo simulations in emission tomography.
the use of Monte Carlo simulations to predict the performance of emission tomographs in realistic clinical situations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the purpose of Monte Carlo simulations, the spatial resolution of the input activity distribution should be as high as possible.
the input data for the simulations should have the same noise properties as clinical data, but higher spatial resolution.

the noise properties in the simulated image are almost independent of the properties of input images, but the spatial resolution in the simulated images is slightly worse than that in the reconstructed input images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Monte Carlo simulation of emission tomography is a powerful tool to study the physical and technical properties of emission tomographs.

, if one wishes to use Monte Carlo simulations to study the impact of a given factor on emission tomography images, one can use the activity distribution obtained from clinical images, even when these images are noisy and have limited spatial and temporal resolution.
the spatial resolution of the activity distribution is not critical in Monte Carlo simulations of clinical emission tomography.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to simulate realistic images, it is not necessary to use the highest spatial resolution available in the input activity maps.
the noise properties in the input activity distributions do not affect the quality of the simulated images.
Monte Carlo simulation of emission tomography is not limited to the study of the detector design and the optimization of acquisition protocols.
